sections.heading: C — Before driving
sections.markdown:
## C — Before driving

FACT_ID: sec04-F01 | anchor: A26
Adjust the driving seat and mirrors before starting to drive. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F02 | anchor: A26
The seating position should allow a clear view and full use of the pedals and steering wheel. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F03 | anchor: A26
Leave room for the airbag to deploy when selecting the driving position. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F04 | anchor: A26
Position the seat so the foot can pivot between brake and accelerator while the heel stays on the floor. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F05 | anchor: A26
Adjust the steering wheel or column if the vehicle provides that adjustment. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F06 | anchor: A26
The top of the steering wheel should stay at or below shoulder height and below the chin. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F07 | anchor: A26
The seat-adjustment paragraph calls for 10 inches between the body and the lower steering wheel. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F08 | anchor: A26
Do not move the seat forward so far that steering becomes difficult. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F09 | anchor: A26
Do not recline so far that reaching the wheel or using the mirrors becomes ineffective. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F10 | anchor: A26
A seat cushion or pedal extensions may help provide a suitable view and reach when needed. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F11 | anchor: A26
Head restraints help protect against whiplash in a rear impact. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F12 | anchor: A26
Whiplash involves neck pain after crash forces move the neck beyond its normal range. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F13 | anchor: A26
Set the head restraint against the back of the head at no lower than ear level. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F14 | anchor: A26
Aim the inside rearview mirror to frame the rear window and show traffic behind. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F15 | anchor: A26
Set a day-and-night mirror for the time of day in which you are driving. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F16 | anchor: A26
For traditional mirror adjustment, first set the seat and sit upright. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F17 | anchor: A26
The traditional left mirror setting shows the vehicle's left edge. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F18 | anchor: A26
The traditional right mirror setting shows the vehicle's right edge. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F19 | anchor: A26
Traditional mirror settings may suit towing or maneuvering larger passenger vehicles in confined spaces. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F20 | anchor: A26
Passenger-car side mirrors are not designed to serve as the method for backing the car. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F21 | anchor: A26
Enhanced mirror adjustment uses a leaned head position while setting the side mirrors. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F22 | anchor: A26
With the enhanced setting, the vehicle's sides are not visible during an ordinary glance at the outside mirrors. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F23 | anchor: A26
The handbook attributes an extra 12 to 16 degrees of viewing area on each side to enhanced mirror adjustment. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F24 | anchor: A26
Enhanced mirror adjustment may not suit every vehicle, so traditional settings may be appropriate. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F25 | anchor: A27
Fasten your safety belt before moving the vehicle. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F26 | anchor: A27
Check that passengers use safety belts or suitable child restraints before departure. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F27 | anchor: A27
Lock the vehicle doors before driving. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F28 | anchor: A27
Use the childproof door locks when children ride in the vehicle. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F29 | anchor: A27
Safety belts lower the chance of injury or death in a crash. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F30 | anchor: A27
Safety belts permit ordinary movement but lock during a crash. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F31 | anchor: A27
A safety belt helps prevent a rider from being ejected or striking the vehicle interior. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F32 | anchor: A27
A safety belt helps a driver remain behind the wheel to retain steering control. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F33 | anchor: A27
Kansas prohibits driving without a safety belt under the law described in this section. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F34 | anchor: A27
Kansas prohibits riding in a front seat without a safety belt under the law described in this section. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F35 | anchor: A27
Wear a safety belt on every trip, including short journeys and lower-speed roads. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0027]

Misconceptions: An airbag supplements a safety belt; its presence does not eliminate the need to buckle up.
Mnemonics: Editorial cue: position, mirrors, restraints; use the cited facts for the actual setup and placement decisions.
Glossary: A head restraint limits rear-impact neck motion; front airbags are supplemental restraints; a shoulder harness is the upper belt portion.
Dynamic facts: Child-seat transition guidance and statutory age boundaries require issuer refresh; ambiguous mirror geometry and undated crash statistics remain typed debt.
